Wait, let me parse carefully.

x0 = objects(I,T,F,T): univalued objects, not diagonal, without background.
x1 = totuple(x0): tuple of objects.
x2 = apply(color, x1): tuple of colors of each object.
x3 = lbind(sfilter, x2): function that filters x2 by condition.
x4 = lbind(matcher, identity): matcher(identity, ...) -> lambda c: identity(c) == ? wait matcher(function, target) returns lambda x: function(x) == target. lbind(matcher, identity) fixes first arg function=identity, so it's lambda target: lambda x: identity(x) == target. Then chain(size, x3, x4) = lambda x: size(x3(x4(x))). Hmm chain(h,g,f)=lambda x: h(g(f(x))). So x5 = chain(size, x3, x4) = lambda target: size(sfilter(x2, matcher(identity,target))) = number of objects whose color == target.

x6 = matcher(x5, ONE) = lambda c: x5(c) == 1, i.e., colors c such that exactly one object has color c.

x7 = sfilter(x2, x6): colors appearing in exactly one object.

x8 = lbind(colorcount, I): lambda c: colorcount(I, c).

x9 = argmax(x7, x8): the color among those appearing in exactly one object with the highest count in the grid. Since exactly one object has that color, that's the largest object among colors that are unique (appear in only one object).

x10 = matcher(color, x9): find object with that color.

x11 = extract(x0, x10). x12 = subgrid(x11, I).
